subQuests.subQuestName: Take a look around the Court of Fontaine

140300101.text: The wait is over, everyone! The sale of our new skincare product, Romaritime Essence, will now begin!

140300102.text: Another skincare promotion? And it's selling as fast as last time! Wonder what people would think if they knew what was in that last batch...

140300105.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, hello! I hope you two got a good rest yesterday after all your hard work?

140300106.text: Of course! Nurse's orders, right? ...Anyway, are you here to take notes for your next article?

140300107.text: Actually, I'm mostly here to help Officer Morgane wrap up yesterday's case.

140300108.text: Ah, that reminds Paimon... That stuff sold like crazy, didn't it! Is it gonna cause huge problems?

140300109.text: Nope, there's nothing to worry about. Unless modified, Butterfly Dew is an excellent skincare product that's completely safe to use.

140300110.text: Besides, officers have already retrieved all Butterfly Dew purchased on the market. Now, it's just a matter of disposal.

140300111.text: After consulting Monsieur Neuvillette, I came up with a way to neutralize any harmful effects, so it'll evaporate naturally without polluting the water or soil.

140300112.text: Wow! It's Sigewinne to the rescue again!

140300113.text: Thank you for serving as our consultant, Head Nurse. All the Butterfly Dew we recovered has been disposed of according to your instructions.

140300115.text: Also, you mentioned you wanted a copy of Rawat's interrogation records... Well, technically Potton's records... Anyway, I have them with me. Here.

140300116.text: After he saw his mother for the last time, it was like all his mental defenses came crashing down. He put up no resistance during the interrogation, and answered all our questions. We learned a lot.

140300117.text: Apparently, the formula was something he discovered by chance while helping the criminal gang produce Sinthe. Later, he came up with the idea to dilute it and use the resulting substance as a skincare product.

140300118.text: Their supplier was Vacher — but you could also argue that they were the ones doing him a favor. His operation helped Vacher's gang dispose of an enormous amount of evidence.

140300119.text: It made for a seamless collaboration. One man's trash was another man's treasure, and there were no loose ends. It's no wonder we never noticed what Potton's gang was up to.

140300120.text: Vacher again, huh... Is there still no end to the harm he caused?

140300121.text: Make no mistake, the crimes of Vacher and his accomplices will come to an end. It's only a matter of time.

140300122.text: Since the flood cut off their supply of Primordial Seawater, they've been forced to resort to riskier methods — like using their private reserve to attack people on the street. Naturally, those attempts all ended in failure.

140300123.text: After receiving numerous reports, we were able to zero in on the gang and eventually round them up.

140300125.text: Based on what he told us in his confession, we pretty much had him backed into a corner, even though he made a point of distancing himself from the gang while disguised as Rawat.

140300126.text: He tried to throw us off his tail by reporting his accomplices, giving him enough time to transform back into Potton and see his mother one last time.

140300127.text: But, there was one thing he hadn't anticipated... Even though "Potton" had been missing for a long time, we were very much still on the lookout for him. So the moment he appeared in public after changing back to his original appearance, we caught him.

140300128.text: So he tried this once before, huh? Guess he really did want his mother to see him again. But in the end...

140300129.text: ...Looking at the interrogation records, it seems like he spent the first sum of money he earned as Rawat on his mother's treatment.

140300130.text: Yes, which is why I suspect that his initial motive for using the potion was not personal greed, but a desire to become somebody who had the power to save her.

140300131.text: Even so, he went too far. In the end, he got what he deserved.

140300132.text: I understand. Thank you for bringing me these records.

140300133.text: Why did you want them, anyway?

140300134.text: Potton was one of my patients, so I need to put together a medical file for him. My teacher always stressed that a person's life experiences are just as important to their file as their medical history.

140300135.text: Why are you still treating him like your patient? Isn't he kinda beyond redemption now?

140300136.text: That may be true, but a patient is a patient, regardless of the choices that bring them to my care.

140300137.text: Ah, one last thing, Head Nurse. Please keep everything you know about this potion a secret.

140300138.text: It would be for the best if most of Fontaine knows nothing of its existence. I know my fellow officers and I will be able to sleep easier if that's the case.

140300140.text: Thank you for understanding. I'll take my leave, then.

140300141.text: So Sigewinne, did you really use that potion yourself?

140300142.text: Why do you sound so surprised, Paimon? I told you all about it. It was quite a while ago now.

140300143.text: Uhh... You mean that story about the witch and the potion? So it was really, actually, genuinely a true story?

140300144.text: Yes. It really, actually, genuinely was.

140300146.text: The process of making that potion...

140300147.text: I know. There are some secrets I can't tell anyone about. But considering everything we've been through together, I know I can trust you with them.

140300148.text: Before I tell you, though, could you follow me somewhere? I want to pay my respects to an old friend.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the place you agreed upon with Sigewinne

140300201.text: Oh... Neuvillette and Wriothesley! They're here too!

140300202.text: #Good to see you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. I trust all has been going well for you.

140300203.text: Big news, everyone: The Iudex is out of his office on important business.

140300204.text: Hmm? Is that genuinely something people would consider "big news"?

140300205.text: Why wouldn't they? Important business is a big deal.

140300206.text: Ah... Yes, you're quite right. When someone you care about requires emotional support, being there for them at the right time and place is of the utmost importance.

140300256.text: After reading the Marechaussee Phantom's reports, I had a feeling a trip here might be in order.

140300207.text: Take note — that, my friends, is how Monsieur Neuvillette shows that he cares. We're both here for the same purpose, actually — to accompany Sigewinne as she pays her respects to her late teacher.

140300208.text: So the old friend she mentioned was her teacher then? The "witch"?

140300209.text: Uh, sorry, sorry, Paimon didn't mean to be rude! It's only 'cause Sigewinne calls her that all the time, so...

140300210.text: I doubt she considers that title to be offensive, Paimon. Don't worry.

140300211.text: Indeed. In fact, I believe Sigewinne would take it as a sign of affection. She has spoken of this doctor on many occasions, and it sounds like she was a truly generous individual.

140300212.text: In those days, many people harbored prejudices against Melusines. She was the only teacher willing to take Sigewinne on as a student.

140300213.text: Wow, it's really nice of you two to be here for Sigewinne! Guess you guys really look out for your younger colleagues, huh...

140300214.text: Younger colleague? That might be true for the Iudex, but I'm not sure I can say the same.

140300215.text: Sigewinne served a sentence in the Fortress of Meropide hundreds of years ago, and after she did her time, she decided to stick around. She's been an integral part of our administration ever since.

140300216.text: Strictly speaking, the head nurse has been around longer than most people in the Fortress, myself included. Pretty sure that makes me the younger colleague.

140300219.text: Yes. Long before I became Iudex, there was an ancient law in Fontaine that prohibited any attempt to transform another species into a human.

140300220.text: Initially, I and most researchers believed this law to have been imposed due to ethical concerns.

140300221.text: But now, it seems more likely that the law was nothing more than an insurance policy — a way for Egeria to ensure that her people would remain insulated from the truth, thus enabling them to lead more straightforward, happier lives.

140300222.text: Ignorance is bliss, as they say.

140300223.text: Sigewinne had her reasons for choosing to obtain a human form, but the act was nonetheless in clear violation of the law.

140300224.text: Could you tell us a bit more about what happened back then?

140300225.text: Certainly. Sigewinne does not object to her close friends learning about her history. In fact, I first learned of it myself because she confessed the truth to me of her own volition...

140300226.text: Even with their daughter so ill, they kicked you out? Stubborn as always... and prejudice isn't a disease I can cure, either.

140300227.text: *sigh* Shame that I don't have the energy to get over there. You're laughable, you old witch. You want to save everyone in Fontaine, but you can't even save the patient before you.

140300229.text: I discovered a strange disease, one I suspect that every Fontainian suffers from. But without witnesses or proof, no one will believe me.

140300230.text: I had no choice but to experiment on myself to find a cure, but I hit a wall — and as you can see, it took a wretched toll on me.

140300231.text: Then... I'll find a cure for you, and then you can go cure her!

140300232.text: There's no need... I'm beyond saving now. There's nothing you can do.

140300234.text: As I said before, a doctor's duty is to treat whatever ailments they can.

140300235.text: I know... But, they don't trust me at all.

140300236.text: *cough* That girl... She's your first ever patient, isn't she? ...Tell me, what cost are you willing to bear to see her cured?

140300238.text: Even if it means breaking the law and being punished for it?

140300239.text: ...As long as I don't hurt anyone, yes.

140300240.text: Haha. Spoken like a true student of mine.

140300241.text: Then I shall make one more final gamble... and see my experiment through to its end. Leave me for now, and come back in two hours.

140300242.text: If I am able to work this miracle, then I will have found a way to save all Fontainians, and I shall be able to help you treat that girl.

140300243.text: If not... Then it means there is one more disease in this world that I cannot treat. In that case, do not come looking for me.

140300244.text: I will leave you a parting gift — an accidental discovery, happened upon through my study of this strange disease. It has little use, but it will at least help you cure this one patient you can reach.

140300245.text: When Sigewinne returned, the miracle had not occurred.

140300246.text: She found a potion bottle and a note on the table. After using the potion as instructed, she gained her current form, breaking Fontaine's law in the process.

140300247.text: And after I had confirmed the veracity of the events, I gave my verdict.

140300302.text: The old friend I mentioned was my teacher. When she passed, her body was nowhere to be found. All that's left of her is an empty tomb, and even that's deep underwater now.

140300303.text: Sigewinne... The witch who gave you the magic potion, she was your teacher, wasn't she?

140300304.text: Ah, sounds like Monsieur Neuvillette filled you in.

140300305.text: After learning the truth... it must've been hard to process, huh?

140300306.text: Well... To be honest, after I realized what really happened that night, my first thought was that it kind of made sense. It seemed exactly like the sort of thing she would do.

140300307.text: But, she was planning to sacrifice herself, and never told you!

140300308.text: That's just who she was. If lying is what it took to get a kid to take their medicine, then that's what she'd do.

140300311.text: Alright... But, why did you turn yourself in?

140300312.text: I broke the law, simple as that. My teacher made her choice, and I made mine.

140300313.text: True, it's just... The way Potton framed it when he was asking you all those questions, it made Paimon really mad!

140300314.text: You're not like him at all, and everything Neuvillette said confirms that...

140300315.text: And yet you were still convicted and thrown in prison... It just feels so unfair.

140300316.text: Unfair? I happen to think just the opposite. If I hadn't served that time, I'm not sure I would've been able to stay strong when he was questioning me.

140300318.text: I knew you'd be curious. Let me tell you a story...

140300319.text: Now that's an ending Paimon can get behind!

140300320.text: After hearing everything Potton said, I wanted to tell him that it didn't matter who he looked like on the outside... But it was too late — the warmth in his palm had already disappeared.

140300321.text: I tried to treat him, but... The roots of his problem had nothing to do with his face.

140305101.text: On behalf of the Marechaussee Phantom, I would like to once again thank the Fortress of Meropide for your assistance in the response to yesterday's prisonbreak.

140305102.text: #Our Head Nurse and {NICKNAME} and Paimon did most of the heavy lifting, I would say.

140305103.text: Sigewinne seems to be in good spirits. I trust work hasn't been too hard on her lately?

140305104.text: Well, she might be the only permanent medical staff in the Fortress, but there's plenty of people with medical knowledge willing to help her out.

140305105.text: I am most relieved to hear it.

140305106.text: Haha, the way you're asking after her wellbeing makes you sound like a concerned parent.

140305107.text: Ah, well, I won't lie... I've always seen myself that way.

140305108.text: Showing your age a bit there, don't you think...

140305109.text: Indeed. Actually, I often forget just how much older I am than you...

140305110.text: Well, while we're on the topic... What did you do before getting this job, anyway? Spend all day swimming in the sea, from east to west, then north to south?

140305111.text: Yes, and uh... from the surface to the ocean floor, on occasion.

140305113.text: ...Apologies, that was merely an attempt at humor. You can disregard what I said.

140305114.text: Hah, that's impossible, I'm afraid. My imagination's already running wild.

140305201.text: I'd like to stay here with my teacher for a little longer.

140305301.text: Stocks are running low, so purchase soon to avoid disappointment!

140309801.text: Potton is eventually taken away by members of the Marechaussee Phantom. A day passes in a flash.
